Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers and the private deployment options look promising. Procurement asked me to get a concrete commercial proposal that addresses two things up front: 1) a hybrid private-offer pricing model (base seat commit + metered overage for inference) and 2) an explicit channel margin/passback waterfall so our reseller (HealthBridge) can invoice correctly.

Specific asks from procurement:
- 12-month term, ability to smooth commit across quarters if usage is lumpy
- an overage cap or credit mechanism for the first 90 days of ramp
- clarity on list price vs marketplace private-offer price and resulting reseller margin
- a sample clause they can include in the PO about true-ups and smoothing

Can you send a short term-sheet and the channel margin waterfall by next Wednesday? If you need any procurement contacts, I'm looping in nimbus-sales (nimbus-sales@nhc.com).

Best,
Kate Liu

Nimbus Health Corporation

Hi Kate —

Appreciate the clear list. I've put together a short term-sheet and a sample channel waterfall (attached) that addresses the smoothing/overage concern. Executive summary up front:
- Proposed commercial: 12-month Private Offer (Azure private catalog) with a hybrid billing profile: 250 committed seats at $X/seat-month + metered inference token usage at $Y per 1k tokens above commit.
- Commit smoothing: quarterly true-up with a 10% smoothing buffer that allows Nimbus to move up to +/-10% of quarterly committed seats without immediate penalty; annual true-up reconciles the delta.
- Ramp protection: for the first 90 days we offer a 30% overage credit on metered usage beyond commit (reduces overage rate) to de-risk launch.
- Channel margin: we propose a 10% passback to HealthBridge off the private-offer list price, with a 2% holdback applied to the first invoice to cover potential chargebacks; holdback released at 60 days post-implementation if no disputes.

I've attached: 1) Nimbus-Term-Sheet-draft-v1.pdf — short commercial bullets and numbers, 2) channel-waterfall-example.xlsx — simple waterfall that shows list price -> private-offer discount -> reseller passback -> net to Redwood. Ben / Olga — can you confirm the holdback mechanics are ok from a finance/tax perspective?

If that looks reasonable, I'll turn this into a single-sheet DocuSign and sample clause for procurement.

Thanks,
Logan Wright

Logan / team — quick finance notes after reviewing the waterfall:
- The 10% passback is fine, but procurement will want the netback example after tax and marketplace fees. For Azure private offers the marketplace fee shapes differently depending on whether we route via marketplace listing or reseller-managed purchase. Please add two scenarios in the waterfall: (A) private-offer via marketplace (marketplace fee 6%) and (B) off-market private offer (no marketplace fee but different invoicing).
- Holdback mechanics: a 2% initial holdback is operationally okay, but we should limit exposure by capping absolute dollars (e.g., max $25k holdback) and include dispute resolution timeline (30 days to raise disputes, 60 days to clear).
- Overage credit: 30% credit is generous; can we make it tiered: 30% credit for months 0-1, 20% for month 2, 10% month 3? That reduces risk for us.

I've updated the spreadsheet (see channel-waterfall-example.xlsx) with two scenarios and the capped holdback column. I've not attached the updated file to this thread to keep file size small — will drop into the HubSpot deal.

-Ben

Kate —

Attached is a consolidated package: "Nimbus-Term-Sheet-draft-v1.pdf" now includes: the commercial bullets, the invoice-level smoothing language, and the 90-day tiered overage credit mechanics. The XLSX contains Scenario A/B netbacks and a column showing list price vs private-offer SKU price for HealthBridge. Highlights and the requested sample clause below (you can paste it into the PO):

Sample smoothing / overage clause (editable):
"During the first 12 months of the Agreement, Customer shall purchase the committed seats per quarter as set forth in the applicable Order Form. For the first ninety (90) days following the Service Go-Live, any metered usage above the committed threshold shall be eligible for an overage credit applied to the next invoice on a tiered basis: Month 0-30 days: 30% credit, Month 31-60 days: 20% credit, Month 61-90 days: 10% credit. Quarterly invoices will not exceed 110% of the invoiced committed-seat charges for that quarter prior to reconciliation. Annual true-up shall reconcile any remaining variance with netting of credits before additional charges apply. All credits shall be applied as offsets to future invoices and shall not be paid out as cash refunds."

Holdback and dispute timeline: Redwood will apply an initial holdback equal to 2% of the first invoice amount up to a cap of $25,000. Customer shall have thirty (30) days from invoice issuance to submit disputes. Absent timely disputes, holdback funds will be released to the reseller within sixty (60) days.

If that wording looks good, I can request DocuSign and route to legal for a final redline where necessary. Next operational asks from our side:
- Final purchase order or committed-seat numbers (we used 250 as a placeholder)
- Expected Go-Live (we recommended a 6/21/2027 start in the term-sheet)

Kate — thanks again. If you want a quick 20-minute call to walk the procurement/legal team through the clause, Ben and I are available this afternoon.

Best,
